PullRequest.Title: chat: polish progress and inline tool rendering
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #338410

## Summary

- Default persistent progress to Draw for every product quality, retaining explicit configuration overrides.
- Constrain long tool/disclosure titles so they cannot overlap adjacent content. Keep completed-step counts and elapsed time on a single line, with ellipsis and a full-text hover when needed.
- Align subagent tool icons and labels, increase their gap, and reuse the shared read/search/terminal/generic icon lookup.
- Keep the named subagent tool row visible during confirmation. With persistent progress enabled, show the pending-confirmation count only in the footer rather than duplicating it inside the chain.
- Preserve the original read-reference pill markup and visual treatment. Make markdown and external edit pills reuse that compact treatment, including text baseline alignment, visible `+/-` counters, and a small inset after the final count.
- Remove excess padding and disclosure spacing from answered question summaries.
- Cache fixed Draw ribbon geometry without changing the SVG paths, animation timing, or colors. A local frame-generation benchmark improved about 3.4x; 4,106 sampled phases matched the original output exactly.
- Add focused rendering regressions, themed fixtures, and Draw geometry snapshots.

The experimental progress-message fade/roll transitions explored during development are **not included**.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed.
- The following command — **844 passed, 1 pre-existing skipped test**:

  ```sh
  ./scripts/test.sh \
    --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts \
    --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatInlineAnchorWidget.test.ts \
    --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatMarkdownContentPart.test.ts \
    --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatSubagentContentPart.test.ts \
    --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatToolProgressPart.test.ts \
    --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatWorkingLogo.test.ts
  ```

- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts` — passed after the final test-helper change. Other affected TypeScript files were linted during implementation.
- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/media/chatCodeBlockPill.css` — passed after the final count-padding change. Original read-pill spacing is deliberately retained; the linter reports advisory design-token suggestions for those existing values.
- Themed component checks exercised read/edit sizing, baseline alignment, narrow summaries, high contrast, and screenshot stability.
- Earlier recorded Code OSS Dev scenarios passed the subagent confirmation and rendering flows. The latest full-window compact-pill rerun stopped at a keyboard-expansion assertion after its streaming/completed-size and single-line-summary checks passed; that full rerun is not claimed as a pass.

## Manual checks

1. In both narrow and wide chat panels, inspect a completed response with elapsed time and expand its completed steps.
2. Compare read-file pills with markdown/external edit pills; the read appearance should be unchanged, and edits should retain their aligned `+/-` counts and trailing inset.
3. Watch streaming read labels become completed file pills.
4. Trigger a subagent confirmation with persistent progress enabled, then switch progress Off and back to Draw.
5. Inspect answered question spacing and the Draw animation in light, dark, high-contrast, and reduced-motion modes.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The default-resolution and render call path are directly traced, and the rAF loop plus path generation are explicit. Visibility and completion guards bound the work to visible active responses, and fixed-band caching lowers each frame's cost; only the exact milliseconds and device-level impact are uncertain, which is reflected in severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread geometry calculations, short-lived path strings/arrays, and SVG `d` attribute writes on every animation frame
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The work grows with display refresh rate × the duration of each visible active response × the number of simultaneously visible active chat panes; a 30-second response schedules roughly 1,800 frame callbacks at 60 Hz.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Sustained CPU and allocation/GC pressure during agent responses, consuming frame budget and battery and potentially causing dropped frames on slower clients.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: With no explicit override, Stable resolved `chat.experimental.persistentProgress` to `Off`; `isPersistentProgressEnabled()` was false, so `ChatWorkingProgressContentPart` did not construct `ChatWorkingProgressLogo` and there was no JavaScript animation-frame loop or SVG path regeneration. Only Insiders defaulted to Draw.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Stable now resolves the setting to `Draw`. Every visible active persistent-progress footer constructs the Draw logo and continuously runs `getChatWorkingLogoDrawFrame()` from `requestAnimationFrame`, then writes the generated paths into up to three SVG masks.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 15 replaces the Stable-specific `Off` default with unconditional `ChatProgressAnimation.Draw`, newly routing default Stable sessions into the persistent logo's JavaScript rAF/SVG-generation path.
Findings.Title: Avoid defaulting Stable to the per-frame Draw renderer
Findings.Impact: A normal long-running agent request in Stable now performs main-thread SVG geometry generation for its entire visible lifetime. The implementation's own moving-band path remains uncached, so long requests repeatedly allocate and serialize path geometry even after the new fixed-band cache is warm.
Findings.Evidence: The changed default is consumed by `ChatListItemRenderer.isPersistentProgressEnabled()` and passed as `suppressProgressShimmer`; `ChatWorkingProgressContentPart` then creates `ChatWorkingProgressLogo`. Its visible/active path recursively schedules `requestAnimationFrame`; `renderDrawFrame` calls `getChatWorkingLogoDrawFrame` and updates SVG `d` attributes. During tie/untie phases, `Ribbon.bands` builds Maps/arrays and long path strings, and the changed implementation explicitly notes that moving endpoints are never cached. There are no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundaries on this path; the regression is synchronous rendering CPU compared with Stable's prior Off path.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep Stable's default at `Off` (or the no-icon persistent mode) until Draw has an absolute frame-cost budget, or throttle/coalesce path regeneration to a bounded cadence while preserving the same animation and existing visibility/completion guards.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Every visible animation frame rebuilt identical full-band geometry and long SVG path strings for marks wholly inside the revealed ribbon interval.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: The Draw animation incurred avoidable geometry CPU and string allocations at display-frame frequency; the new finite cache removes the unchanged portion of that work.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Fully covered marks now reuse one of four cap-specific path strings from a bounded cache, while only genuinely moving endpoints call strip.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: ChatWorkingLogo calls getChatWorkingLogoDrawFrame from a recursive requestAnimationFrame loop. In the base revision, Ribbon.bands generated each visible mark by calling strip on every moving frame, including fully covered marks whose geometry and cap flags were unchanged. Blame ties that repeated frame-path work to the animation-introducing commit. The PR adds a finite per-mark path cache and uses it whenever the full mark is covered.

Scenarios.Scenario: A Stable user runs a normal visible agent request with no explicit persistent-progress override.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration resolves during response rendering; the new Draw default enables persistent progress, constructs ChatWorkingProgressLogo, and the visible active logo recursively schedules requestAnimationFrame. Each frame must synchronously generate the current ribbon paths and update SVG mask `d` attributes before that frame's rendering; this work is on the UI critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Display refresh rate multiplied by response duration and visible active chat-pane count; one 30-second response is about 1,800 callbacks at 60 Hz.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One serialized rAF loop per visible active working logo; IntersectionObserver/document visibility and response completion stop hidden or inactive loops. Multiple simultaneously visible active chat panes add independent loops with no shared limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The singleton Ribbon has a bounded warm cache for fully covered fixed bands after this PR. Moving endpoints are deliberately not cached, so every tie/untie frame still allocates geometry collections and path strings. Stable's prior Off default bypassed the logo and this frame cache/path entirely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed configuration default, persistent-render branch, logo construction, visibility gate, recursive rAF, geometry generation, and SVG writes were all traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact milliseconds per frame and prevalence of multiple visible chat panes are not measured here; the rAF work and Stable before/after path are certain, so uncertainty affects severity rather than mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium CPU/rendering regression: the diff newly routes default Stable sessions from no JavaScript Draw loop to continuous main-thread geometry and SVG updates for every visible active response.

Scenarios.Scenario: An Insiders user, or a user with an explicit Draw override, watches the existing Draw animation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The animation's rAF callback calls getChatWorkingLogoDrawFrame before writing SVG path attributes. The PR's invariant caches execute directly on this per-frame path and reduce work before the browser can paint.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Frame count over the visible active lifetime; effective cardinality is the finite set of ribbon marks and at most four cap variants per mark.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized per-logo requestAnimationFrame callbacks; no worker, queue, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold construction precomputes each Span's vertex fractions and lazily fills fixed-band cap variants. Warm frames reuse those invariant arrays/path strings; moving endpoint geometry remains uncached. Cache size is bounded by the fixed mark set and is process-lifetime singleton state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: source tracing proves the repeated work and the blamed introducing commit; the regression-fix signal was recorded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Absolute frame time is not available, but the removed concat/filter/sort and identical full-band strip generation are directly present in the base per-frame call path.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance improvement, not a review finding: the PR removes repeated per-frame CPU/allocation work with bounded caches.

Scenarios.Scenario: A response completes and its tool/edit steps collapse into the completed-response disclosure, including narrow-panel hover text and edit pills.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Response completion synchronously computes visible step count, creates or reuses the disclosure DOM, installs one delayed hover, and may observe edit-diff state. CSS controls wrapping/ellipsis and pill geometry; no external operation blocks completion.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible completed responses and the number of rendered response parts in a collapsed range; virtualized/offscreen responses do not create simultaneous hover work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One disclosure per rendered response template. Existing-disclosure checks avoid rebuilding unchanged disclosures, and the template DisposableStore clears hover/listener/autorun resources when the disclosure is replaced or removed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No data cache is added. The hover/listener lifecycle is tied to completedResponseDisclosureDisposables, so rerenders do not retain an unbounded series of hovers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the render and cleanup paths; no expensive boundary was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large transcripts can increase the existing content scan, but this diff adds only one bounded hover registration and CSS/markup changes; it does not increase scan cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added UI work is bounded per visible disclosure and disposed on rebuild/removal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Subagent tools transition into and out of confirmation/authentication while activity labels and icons update.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Observable tool-state changes synchronously normalize a label, infer/compare an icon, update bounded presentation maps, and update existing DOM. Persistent progress suppresses a duplicate confirmation placeholder, reducing rather than adding DOM work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of active child tools and their state/icon-data transitions; effective work per transition is constant aside from short label normalization.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One autorun per tracked active child tool, disposed on completion/replacement through the existing tracking map. State transitions are event-driven rather than per-frame, and UI updates remain serialized on the renderer thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Presentation maps retain only active/recent tool entries and existing disposal logic removes completed/replaced trackers. The changed generic-label cleanup deletes temporary entries; no unbounded cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the state autorun and cleanup trace; no subprocess/IPC/filesystem/database/network boundary is invoked by these rendering changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agents may have varying child-tool counts, but the changed icon comparison and label fallback are constant-time, low-frequency operations relative to tool events.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: changed work is bounded and low-frequency, with cleanup preserved.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 23 changed files and every diff page. Submitted one Stable-default Draw CPU/rendering finding and recorded the PR's bounded Draw geometry cache as a regression fix; other UI, lifecycle, and styling changes were bounded and introduced no expensive-boundary fan-out.
